title: Comparative evaluation result
description: The output of one evaluation run. Productivity is reported as a vector, never a single number. Setting, study stage, identification, and review status are recorded separately and cannot by themselves promote a positive evidence state.

record_kind.description: A template is an explicitly unexecuted prospective record; only a result can enter live-assurance recomputation.

task_set.description: Identifier of the registered task set the arms were run on.

setting.description: Where and with whom the evaluation occurred; this is not an identification claim.

study_stage.description: The prospectively declared purpose and maturity of the study.

identification.description: How, if at all, the contrast supports attribution.

review_status.description: Who has assessed the complete, hash-bound study artifact.

claim_boundary.description: The population, workflow, model, protocol version, setting, and outcome boundary to which any conclusion is limited.

decision.description: Required by the validator before a positive evidence state can be claimed. The observed difference is always agent_with_protocol minus agent_without_protocol.

blocking_regressions.description: Material safety, quality, cost, burden, or accessibility regressions that block a net-gain conclusion.

arms.description: One entry per comparison arm. A benchmark design may run only the two agent arms; a controlled/field design should include the no-agent baseline where feasible.

arm.description: Which of the three arms this is.

n.description: Number actually observed in this arm; use zero, not a fictional one, when an arm was not run.

acceptance_pass_rate.description: Fraction of tasks whose fresh output passed the acceptance graders (0..1).

taskset_passed.description: True when the agent_with_protocol arm's FRESH outputs passed the acceptance tests on this live run — the evidence that justifies the TASKSET_PASSED assurance rung.

runner.description: Provenance binding the result to a runner, exact pack metadata, both intervention prompts, registered tasks, captured outputs, and source identity. Schema-version 1.0 records are preserved historical evidence; newly produced schema-version 2.0 records require the complete binding.

tasks_sha256.description: Hash of the task-set inputs + graders.

outputs_sha256.description: Hash of the captured raw outputs file.

task_ids.description: Ordered identifiers of the task subset actually run; a partial subset cannot earn the full task-set assurance rung.

evaluation_cost_usd.description: Judge/evaluation overhead, reported separately from the operational model cost in each arm's productivity vector.

effective_prompt_sha256.description: Hash of the exact prefix extracted from the arm file and prepended to every task input.

dirty.description: Schema-v2 result records require false: the exact inputs must have been committed before the run began. Templates may describe a dirty development checkout but cannot earn live assurance.

limitations.description: What this evaluation does not establish. Required for any design above benchmark.

implied_evidence_status.description: The evidence-ladder state this result records. Candidate v0.2 disables automatic positive promotion; negative and no-evidence states remain recordable.

vector.description: The productivity vector. Report every dimension you measured; leave the rest null rather than guessing. Do not collapse into a scalar unless weights are declared for a specific decision.

completion.description: Fraction of tasks completed to the acceptance standard (0..1).

accuracy.description: 1 minus material-error rate (0..1); material errors and unsupported claims.

human_effort_min.description: Active human minutes: attention, interventions, review.

rework.description: Corrections required after first delivery (count or fraction).

cognitive_burden.description: User-rated difficulty/interruption load (normalised 0..1; lower is better).

accessibility.description: Success rate across differing skill levels/assistive needs (0..1).

safety_events.description: Privacy events, unintended external actions, policy violations. Any non-zero value is a headline, not a footnote.
